claims.statement: Sincich et al. recorded extracellularly in the lateral geniculate nucleus of six anaesthetised, paralysed macaques with amplification sufficient to resolve, in 37 neurons, the synaptic potentials driven by a single retinal ganglion cell together with the relay cell's own spikes, while the receptive-field centre was stimulated with a naturalistic luminance sequence varying at 80 Hz. studies.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

studies.finding: Trace and place protocols increase previously labeled dentate-cell counts and reduce total pyknotic profiles. Other tasks and late-label counts retain null outcomes. Survival and functional necessity remain distinct mechanistic questions.
limitations: Adult male Sprague Dawley rats weighed 300-350 g; chronological age is not stated. Group sizes are generally five or six. The paper does not provide a complete animal manifest or randomized assignment procedure. Coded histology is reported, not complete blinding of every procedure.

BrdU was 200 mg/kg; the injection route is not specified. In the main experiments labeling occurred one week before four consecutive training days, with separate terminal cohorts 24 hours or seven days after training. The approximate three-week label-age wording does not exactly specify elapsed days. Separate sacrificed cohorts do not track individual cells longitudinally.

Trace conditioning used 200 trials per day for four days, an 83-dB 250-ms noise, a 500-ms gap and a 100-ms 0.7-mA shock. Unpaired rats received the same stimulus counts without explicit pairing. All paired animals reached 60% conditioned responses; none of the unpaired animals did. Complete naive-group electrode and handling matching is not specified.

Delay conditioning uses a 320-ms noise coterminating with an 80-ms shock and a different conditioned-response window. Trace and delay differ in stimulus durations and scoring as well as temporal gap. The reported F(1,19)=4.24, P=0.05 is called nonsignificant; this boundary result and final-day similarity are not statistical equivalence.

Place training uses a fixed submerged platform, cue training a visible platform moved among quadrants, with four trials per day for four days. Swim controls are yoked to place-training swim duration without a platform; their interval includes the omitted platform-rest time. Time matching does not establish identical stress, motivation or hormone exposure.

Hippocampal dependence is imported from prior lesion literature and, for the exact rat trace protocol, unpublished lesion data. No matched hippocampal lesion or selective newborn-cell manipulation is performed in this histology study. The graph links the specified task protocol to its measured outcome, not generic hippocampal necessity.

At 24 hours after training, prelabelled dentate BrdU counts are elevated after trace conditioning (F(2,15)=137.40, P=0.0001) and place training (F(3,20)=266.40, P=0.0001); Figure 1b/f gives six rats per group. Exact endpoint means are not tabulated and have not been digitized. The abstract doubling language is not an exact universal multiplier or an edge weight.

Delay conditioning has no detected BrdU-count increase (F(2,12)=1.889, P=0.1936); cue training and time-yoked swimming also lack the reported place-training increase. Nonsignificance is neither equivalence nor absence of a smaller effect. These selected tasks and controls do not prove that all possible learning or stress is irrelevant.

The late-labeling trace cohort receives BrdU on the final training day after learning criterion, followed by tissue collection 24 hours later. F(2,13)=0.011, P=0.9892 concerns that retained-label count, not every phase of proliferation throughout training or a direct instantaneous mitotic rate.

Subgranular pyknotic profiles are defined morphologically, not by neuron-specific birthdated identity. Trace means are 220.0 +/- 41.9 naive, 81.8 +/- 24.3 paired and 214.8 +/- 46.5 unpaired; the printed F(3,15)=12.339, P=0.0007 gives a numerator degree of freedom inconsistent with three ordinary ANOVA groups. No corrected statistic is substituted.

Place-training pyknotic means are 208.7 +/- 30.9 naive, 50.0 +/- 8.4 place, 222.0 +/- 48.1 cue and 236.0 +/- 34.2 swim, with reported F(3,20)=16.527, P=0.0001. The paragraph does not allocate these pyknotic counts unambiguously to the 24-hour or seven-day terminal cohorts. Reduced total pyknosis does not by itself identify survival of the BrdU-positive neuronal population.

BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are rare, reported as 0-36 per dentate gyrus, and not observed after the two selected learning tasks. No BrdU-positive pyknotic profiles are observed in the 24-hour late-labeling cohort. These are detection-limited snapshots of labeled degeneration, not complete survival trajectories.

SVZ sampling excludes the anterior portion and uses sections spanning the dentate gyrus. The trace SVZ null is printed as F(2,15)=0.09 with P=0.3598, an inconsistent ordinary F-test pair. The maze SVZ null is F(3,20)=0.279, P=0.8538. Neither result establishes absence throughout the SVZ or brain.

Granule-cell-layer volume has no detected group difference in trace (F(2,15)=0.043, P=0.958) or maze (F(3,20)=0.302, P=0.8236) comparisons. Gross regional volume is not the count of newborn neurons, a measured replacement balance or an equivalence test.

The seven-day post-training groups are reported to retain elevated BrdU counts, without a separate endpoint figure, table or test. Marker proportions at that endpoint are approximately 57% TOAD-64, 11% GFAP and 71% calbindin among BrdU-labeled cells. Separate overlapping marker assays must not be summed into a cell-type partition.

Marker comparisons report F(3,20)=0.311, P=0.8169 for TOAD-64 and identical F(3,20)=0.572, P=0.6402 for GFAP and calbindin. Exact assay/cohort allocation and the duplicated statistics require raw data; they are not silently repaired. Minimum sampling is 50 labeled cells per animal on at least six sections, with confocal verification.

Counts use coded slides, every twelfth 40-micrometre coronal section and exclusion of the outermost focal plane. Pyknotic counts use the same modified optical fractionator; volume uses Cavalieri estimation. Processed thickness, raw counts, optical stacks and analysis code are unavailable. Statistical methods specify Neuman Keuls comparisons.

The control time course rises from two hours to one week and falls by two weeks after labeling, but involves separate terminal cohorts. The survival interpretation also draws on prior autoradiographic grain counts and unpublished observations. The authors explicitly cannot exclude proliferation; a unique survival mechanism is not experimentally isolated.

No newborn-cell necessity, selective rescue, synaptic-output or memory-storage test is performed. Untrained controls retain labeled cells, and the authors leave unspecified natural learning as a possible contributor to baseline survival. The study establishes neither a universal learning prerequisite nor its universal absence, and no primate or human generalization follows.
